Definition: of Hebrew origin (H1904); Hagar, the concubine of Abraham:--Hagar.
BiblicalUsage: Agar is Hagar, the concubine of Abraham — and Paul uses her name in his allegory of the two covenants. Hagar stands for Mount Sinai and the covenant of bondage, bearing children who are slaves; Sarah stands for the Jerusalem above, the mother of the free.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Paul's use of Hagar is a warning I need to hear: the way of the law is the way of the slave, and it cannot make anyone free. The children of the promise are born of the free woman, and I belong to that line by faith, not by my own efforts.
RelatedEvents: Hagar and Ishmael; The Binding of Isaac
